title: Choose where PCSX2 stores portable data from the command line
summary: Compare PCSX2’s `-portable` and `-datapath` switches in a temporary launch, noting that `-portable` takes precedence over `-datapath`.

author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: select pcsx2 portable data folder with cli switches
Choose where PCSX2 stores portable data from the command line

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents `-portable` as forcing data storage in the local PCSX2 path instead of the normal configuration directory. It also documents `-datapath <path>` as choosing a directory for application data, but explicitly says `-portable` overrides `-datapath`. Choosing the wrong launch shortcut can therefore make a separate test appear to ignore its requested data directory.

Close PCSX2 and locate the executable directory and your existing configuration directory. Back up any settings you need before testing. Create a new empty folder for the test data and do not point the experiment at a removable drive that may disconnect. This procedure changes where a launched instance reads and writes emulator data; it does not move BIOS or game files.

items: 1. Make a copy of the PCSX2 launch shortcut or command so the normal launch remains available.
2. First test `-datapath` by itself, followed by the empty test directory path.
3. Launch once, confirm PCSX2 opens, close it normally, and inspect whether its expected application data appeared in that test directory.
4. Next add `-portable` before `-datapath` in the copied launch command and start once more.
5. Inspect the local PCSX2 folder; the documented precedence means portable mode should use that local path rather than the explicit datapath.
6. Close the test instance and write down which folder it actually used before importing or changing settings.

blocks.text: The check passes when the application starts and the new files appear in the directory predicted by the active switch. With `-portable`, expect the local PCSX2 path; with only `-datapath`, expect the specified path. Do not treat a shortcut’s target text as proof: inspect the resulting files after a clean close.

items: No test files appear: make sure PCSX2 closed normally and you inspected the correct user-data location.
The wrong path receives files: check for `-portable`, which overrides `-datapath`.
An old config appears: the launch shortcut may still point to the normal data directory.
A removable path disappears: close the emulator and restore a stable local path before continuing.

blocks.text: Close PCSX2, remove the temporary launch switches from the copied shortcut, and return to the normal launcher. Keep or delete the empty test folder only after confirming it contains no saves or configuration you want. Never delete the established PCSX2 data folder to force the test to succeed.
